effective_date_basis: The earliest of: own terms, a superseding order, the Commonwealth transition, X1-E4.
ending_pattern: Candidate ends, earliest first: the inauguration of the Commonwealth (Nov. 15, 1935, under the Tydings-McDuffie Act, 48 Stat. 456) for orders about the Governor General and insular administration; the transfer of the Bureau of Insular Affairs to Interior (Reorganization Plan No. II of 1939); and independence on July 4, 1946 (Proclamation 2695; event X1-E4). For reservations, the U.S.-sovereign status of an executive-order reservation is a candidate end on July 4, 1946; later U.S. use of bases rested on the 1946 treaty and the Military Bases Agreement of March 14, 1947, a new basis, not a continuation of the order.

exceptions_savings.assessment: Property the United States retained after 1946 (embassy, cemeteries, veterans' facilities) under later agreements: independent bases.

legal_effect: Research pattern only. A type rule never fills a judgment field, establishes an end, a date, a status or savings for any order, and never substitutes for reading the order's own text.
outlier_conditions: The order's own text (not only the WPA summary or APP title) does not match the type, or the held text is another order's.
The order does more than the type's single act (a second operative clause of another kind).
A later order or statute amends, extends, revokes or revives it before the candidate end.
The order states its own effective date, duration, condition or termination that differs from the pattern.
Orders whose Philippine mention is incidental (for example a civil-service schedule covering many places).
Wartime occupation 1942-45 (government in exile): not an end.

The exemplar's date: the rule's source page and the held text disagree (September 16 vs September 19, 1916); settle from an official printing.
quoted_clause: Under this provision hereafter all official reports which the GovernorGeneral of the Philippine Islands may be required to make of the transactions of the Government of the Philippine Islands will be made to the War Department, and all matters pertaining to the Government of the Philippine Islands, except as otherwise provided by law, are placed in the jurisdiction of that department.
